summary.en: Y Combinator, founded in March 2005 in San Francisco by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Morris and Trevor Blackwell, is the pioneering and most prestigious US seed accelerator. Its standard deal invests $500,000 ($125K for 7% on a post-money SAFE plus a $375K uncapped MFN SAFE) over a 12-week, four-batches-per-year program ending in Demo Day. It has funded more than 5,000 companies with a combined valuation around $600B, including Airbnb, Stripe, Dropbox, Coinbase, DoorDash, Reddit and Instacart.

name.en: SBIR / STTR (Small Business Innovation Research / Small Business Technology Transfer)

strategy.thesis: Congressionally mandated, equity-free federal R&D funding program; 11 participating agencies (DoD, NIH, NASA, DOE, NSF, etc.) award non-dilutive grants/contracts to U.S. small businesses to develop and commercialize innovative technology.

summary.en: SBIR and STTR are the U.S. government's flagship congressionally mandated programs (since 1982) providing equity-free R&D funding to small businesses through 11 federal agencies. Phase I awards run up to ~$323K and Phase II up to ~$2.15M without SBA approval.

summary.en: Archetype is a New York crypto-native venture fund founded in 2021 by Ash Egan. After a $55M Fund I and a $155M Fund II, it raised a $100 million Fund III in 2025, focused on backing early-stage seed rounds of blockchain companies.

summary.en: Lightspeed Faction (Faction) is an early-stage crypto venture firm launched in a joint venture with Lightspeed Venture Partners. It debuted a $285 million inaugural fund (oversubscribed past its $250M target), investing in seed and Series A blockchain startups with $5–10M average checks.

summary.en: Coinbase Ventures is the venture capital arm of Coinbase, founded in 2018. It has made 600+ investments across layer-1 protocols, web3 infrastructure, DeFi, NFTs, and developer tooling, making it one of the most active crypto investors by deal count.
